references.as_reported_note: Savings and accuracy-preservation claims are source-reported only.
references.as_reported_summary: Uses sequence-level entropy from token logprobs as a reasoning early-stopping confidence signal; reports 25-50% computational savings while maintaining task accuracy.
references.relevance: A direct early-stop peer for the Tier-3 fast-path gate, with the important constraint that entropy must be checked against Carnot's verifier signal before becoming a product threshold.
references.title: Think Just Enough: Sequence-Level Entropy as a Confidence Signal for LLM Reasoning

references.as_reported_note: Architecture trends and benchmark outcomes are source-reported only.
references.as_reported_summary: Re-evaluates layer-wise early exit in modern LLMs and reports that newer recipes reduce layer redundancy, making early-exit benefits model- and architecture-dependent.
references.relevance: Cautionary boundary for Tier-3-as-fast-path: fast-path gates should be verifier-calibrated and model-specific, not assumed from older early-exit literature.
references.title: The Diminishing Returns of Early-Exit Decoding in Modern LLMs

references.as_reported_note: Reward-hacking mitigation and theoretical claims are source-reported only.
references.as_reported_summary: Penalizes uncertain out-of-distribution reward estimates in Best-of-N selection; reports substantial mitigation of reward hacking from atypical high-scoring responses.
references.relevance: Concrete mitigation for the banked verifier's reward-gaming surface: use pessimistic uncertainty penalties rather than trusting the highest verifier score under distribution shift.
references.title: From Curiosity to Caution: Mitigating Reward Hacking for Best-of-N with Pessimism

references.as_reported_note: Regret framing and alignment improvements are source-reported only.
references.as_reported_summary: Adapts inference-time alignment to reward-tail heaviness; reports that per-prompt pessimism/optimism interpolation improves alignment relative to fixed reward-model selection rules.
references.relevance: Complements the context-compaction mitigation: verifier routing can treat extreme reward tails as a risk signal instead of blindly expanding compute.
references.title: Best-of-Tails: Bridging Optimism and Pessimism in Inference-Time Alignment

references.as_reported_note: Pipeline outcomes and incentive-equilibrium claims are source-reported only.
references.as_reported_summary: Models solver/auditor oversight as an incentive equilibrium and reports that adaptive reward profiles preserve oversight pressure and reduce hallucinated incorrect attempts in an LLM coding pipeline.
references.relevance: Useful robustness frame for Carnot's banked verifier: score the correction event and auditor inspection incentives, not only the solver's final answer.
references.title: AI Alignment via Incentives and Correction

references.as_reported_note: Risk-coverage and calibration outcomes are source-reported only.
references.as_reported_summary: Finds model-dependent failures of entropy-only abstention and reports improved risk-coverage and calibration from combining entropy with a correctness probe.
references.relevance: Direct banked-abstention product warning: Carnot should privilege verifier/probe-backed abstention over entropy-only routing.
references.title: Entropy Alone is Insufficient for Safe Selective Prediction in LLMs

references.as_reported_note: False-answer and frontier behavior are source-reported only.
references.as_reported_summary: Uses prompt-only confidence elicitation, explicit abstention rewards, and humility norms; reports a coverage-reliability frontier that reduces false answers by shifting error-prone cases to abstention.
references.relevance: Peer abstention-control surface for the banked verifier product, especially where deployment wants a tunable reliability/coverage frontier rather than a single fixed threshold.
references.title: I-CALM: Incentivizing Confidence-Aware Abstention for LLM Hallucination Mitigation

references.as_reported_note: Coverage, risk, and critical-error numbers are source-reported only.
references.as_reported_summary: Introduces information-lift selective-risk certificates and reports 77.0% coverage at 2% risk plus blocking 96% of critical errors in high-stakes scenarios.
references.relevance: Certification route for the banked abstention product: pair Carnot's verifier score with an auditable selective-risk bound.
references.title: Selective Risk Certification for LLM Outputs via Information-Lift Statistics: PAC-Bayes, Robustness, and Skeleton Design

references.as_reported_note: Reasoning and speed/quality tradeoff claims are source-reported only.
references.as_reported_summary: Shows that diffusion LMs use predicted-but-undecoded latent tokens for global coherence and reports a smooth speed/quality tradeoff by modulating how many latent tokens participate.
references.relevance: EDLM-adjacent substrate evidence: the operator-seed route can exploit diffusion's latent-token lookahead instead of repeating the bounded tiny EBT generator path.
references.title: Reasoning with Latent Tokens in Diffusion Language Models

references.as_reported_note: Model size, FLOP, and scaling-law claims are source-reported only.
references.as_reported_summary: Studies scaling laws for discrete diffusion language models and reports a 10B-parameter uniform-diffusion model trained for 10^22 FLOPs while narrowing the likelihood gap at scale.
references.relevance: Scaling precondition for the EDLM operator seed: discrete diffusion is a foundation-model substrate with scale behavior, not merely a small-model generator novelty.
references.title: Scaling Behavior of Discrete Diffusion Language Models

references.as_reported_note: Training-FLOP and reasoning-benchmark gains are source-reported only.
references.as_reported_summary: Loops early-middle masked-diffusion transformer layers and reports up to 3.3x fewer training FLOPs for matched performance plus up to 8.5 GSM8K points from the looped design.
references.relevance: Compute-scaling follow-up for EDLM: recurrent depth and adaptive loop counts give an operator-seed route for test-time compute in masked diffusion without self-seeding the paradigm.
references.title: Looped Diffusion Language Models

references.as_reported_note: Accuracy, latency, and stability figures are source-reported only.
references.as_reported_summary: Prepends an autoregressive natural-language plan to a diffusion LM and reports large reasoning/code gains with stable diffusion inference across seeds.
references.relevance: Operator-seed design hint for EDLM: use an external plan or verifier as globally visible conditioning rather than asking the diffusion model to discover the full reasoning scaffold alone.
references.title: Think First, Diffuse Fast: Improving Diffusion Language Model Reasoning via Autoregressive Plan Conditioning
